summary: Hegemony is a dense, asymmetric economic-political simulation where each player runs a different class with fundamentally different win conditions and mechanisms, engaging in production, labor markets, taxation, and legislative votes across a full economic cycle each round. It plays like a cross between a euro engine-builder and a political simulation, with heavy interlocking systems (loans, contracts, unemployment, class struggle) that reward players who understand macroeconomics.
praised: Deep, believable economic simulation with genuinely asymmetric roles
Legislation/voting system creates real negotiation and shifting alliances
High replayability due to class asymmetry and variable strategies
Satisfying engine-building within each class's distinct toolkit
criticised: Very steep learning curve and long teach time
Long playtime, especially first few plays
Runaway leader potential if one class snowballs economically
Middle class role sometimes seen as less impactful than the other three

interaction.kind: negotiation, trading, and legislative voting alongside competitive market/economic pressure

scoring.why: Each class has its own distinct victory metric (e.g. capital, popularity, wages, budget) determined by that class's economic performance and legislative influence over the game

_name: Hegemony: Lead Your Class to Victory
